summary: Ignazio Abate is an Italian football coach and former full-back. He was born on 12 November 1986. He is head coach of Serie A club Torino. He was naturally a winger, known for stamina and speed. He joined AC Milan's youth system in 1999. He debuted for Milan in December 2003. From 2004 to 2009 he played on loan elsewhere in Italy. Back at Milan in 2009, he became the regular right back. He helped Milan win the 2010–11 Serie A title. He made 306 appearances over ten seasons there. He left as a free agent in July 2019. He retired as a player in 2020. He played at the 2008 Summer Olympics. He debuted for Italy's senior team in November 2011. Italy reached the Euro 2012 final with him. Italy won bronze at the 2013 Confederations Cup. He played at the 2014 World Cup. He coached Milan youth teams from 2021. He managed Serie C club Ternana from 2024. In June 2025, Serie B club Juve Stabia named him head coach.
